chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Juwhari, from Habib al-Khas'ami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Love for the people what you love for yourselves.
ai.seo_question: What is the core ethical principle regarding how Muslims should treat others according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* under the chapter on Justice, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the Golden Rule to a divine imperative, linking personal virtue directly to social equity. It serves as a practical application of *Adl* (justice), urging believers to project their own spiritual and material aspirations onto the community, thereby fostering unity and mutual care. This principle is often cited by Shia scholars as the essence of moral reciprocity, bridging individual piety with communal responsibility.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-23 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Aba Abdullah Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqy, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Juwhary, on the authority of Hubayb al-Khas’ami that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,
“Love for the people what you love for yourselves.”
